content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently underestimate prices in the short term, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Model forecasts show upward bias but fail to capture sharp downward corrections triggered by negative sentiment.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast overshoots, indicating model overconfidence in bullish signals.", "Models exhibit mean-reversion bias, predicting gradual price recovery even when true price drops sharply.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment is mixed or negative, suggesting sentiment interaction is critical for calibration.", "Models lag behind true price movements by 2–3 days, particularly during volatile sentiment shifts.", "Forecasting should incorporate sentiment volatility as a key adjustment factor to avoid persistent underestimation.", "Models overfit recent trends, leading to false confidence in upward trajectories despite historical mean-reversion patterns."]}
